western.temperament: Generous, warm, loyal, bold, big-hearted and theatrical; shadow is pride, vanity, jealousy, bossiness and touchiness.

symbolism.meaning: The first recorded Australian death was in 1954: Kirk Dyson-Holland, a 21-year-old sailor, died within about two hours of a bite (Flecker and Cotton 1955). In 1962 Arthur Ricketts felt 'no sensation of sting or bite' and survived after about an hour of artificial breathing. The painless bite and the need only to keep someone breathing are the real story under the page's 'bite you don't feel'.

In the James Bond film Octopussy the blue-ringed octopus is the emblem of a secret order of women bandits and smugglers. Pop culture, low weight, but it is species-specific and fits Leo glamour over Snake secrecy.

The god Kanaloa is listed as the octopus among the four divinities of the eighth era. Dixon and Bastian read one verse as the octopus being the lone survivor or observer of an earlier world; Beckwith said she reached 'no satisfactory translation'. Octopus in general, not this species. Use with the translation dispute stated, and do not quote the chant itself.

蛸 is the everyday Japanese kanji for octopus, read tako. In Chinese it is mainly a scientific-name character (read shāo), which explains why the page's header looks right to some readers and odd to others.
Page proverb 打草驚蛇 dǎ cǎo jīng shé, 'beat the grass and startle the snake', labeled as Zodi Animal's own pairing. Honest label; keep.
Kiribati octopus god Na Kika, octopus 'spirit animal' meanings, and blue-ringed octopus totem claims: only on godchecker, mythlok and totem blogs. No primary or academic source opened.

fusion.temperament: Our reading: fixed Fire Leo, ruled by the Sun, wants to be seen; yin Fire Snake keeps its counsel. Double Fire with no element to check it, so the heat is real but banked. The blue-ringed octopus fits exactly: plain as rock for weeks, then about 60 rings lit in under a third of a second.
fusion.gifts: Our reading: composure under threat, a signal people believe the first time, loyalty to a small inner circle, strategic patience, the ability to commit totally once.
fusion.shadow: Our reading: flashing at what was never a threat; Leo pride stung, Snake memory long. Or the opposite, staying camouflaged so long nobody counts you in.
fusion.love: Our reading: lets few close, and those few see a warmth strangers never guess. Devoted to the point of self-neglect, like the brooding female that stops eating. Needs a partner who notices the dim rings, not only the flash.
fusion.money: Our reading: Snake materialism under Leo taste. Saves quietly, spends rarely and well; risk is pouring everything into one venture at once.
fusion.conflict: Our reading: retreats and pales first, warns second, strikes last. When it does strike there is no warm-up and no taking it back.

candidate_lines: In the tide pool you pass for rock, and a whole season can go by before anyone learns you were the brightest thing in it.
Your blue comes up in a third of a second, and anyone who has seen it once never asks for a second showing.
Your Leo half wants the open reef; your Snake half picks the crevice. Most nights the crevice wins, and you call it peace.
When someone crosses you, the decision is made before they feel a thing, and by the time they notice, the tide has already turned.
When you finally commit, you curl around it like a brooding mother over her eggs and forget to feed yourself until it hatches.
Strangers in the shallows think you are shy. The few who reach for you learn how much Sun you kept under the sand.

fact_audit.fact: Header hanzi 蛸 on rail and serial, voiced and labeled 'xiāo'
fact_audit.note: 蛸 does mean octopus, but in that sense Mandarin reads it shāo (as in the genus 豹紋蛸屬 bàowén shāo shǔ); xiāo is the reading for 螵蛸 piāoxiāo, the mantis egg case. As a standalone word 蛸 is Japanese (tako) more than Chinese. Best fix: 藍環章魚 lánhuán zhāngyú ('blue-ring octopus', used by Taiwan's National Museum of Natural Science), or keep 蛸 and correct the pinyin and audio to shāo. Dictionary source is unreviewed; a Chinese reader should confirm.

fact_audit.fact: Skin changes color and texture to match rock or coral, via chromatophores controlled by the nervous system
fact_audit.note: Standard cephalopod camouflage. Mäthger et al. add that during the warning display the chromatophores around the rings darken while the body pales.

fact_audit.fact: Rings stay faint until handled or threatened, then flash brilliant iridescent blue as an aposematic warning
fact_audit.note: About 50 to 60 rings flash within a third of a second (Mäthger et al. 2012). Mechanism worth using: the blue comes from iridophores in muscular pockets that open and close, not from pigment. ADW describes the rings as warning coloration.

fact_audit.fact: Saliva carries tetrodotoxin; a bite can go unnoticed; no antivenom
fact_audit.note: Wikipedia: venom includes TTX made by bacteria in the posterior salivary gland; bites 'tiny and often painless'; 'No blue-ringed octopus antivenom is available.' ADW agrees.

fact_audit.fact: Adult greater blue-ringed octopus weighs 10 to 100 grams and measures roughly 10 centimetres
fact_audit.note: Weight 10 to 100 g matches ADW. Length is understated: ADW gives about 20 cm at maximum arm spread; Wikipedia gives 12 to 20 cm for the genus. Rewrite: 'about 12 to 20 cm across the arms'. The phrase 'can weigh as little as 10 to 100 grams' also reads oddly. 'One of the most venomous marine animals' is supported (Wikipedia).

fact_audit.fact: Not aggressive, hides or flees when disturbed; bites almost always defensive after handling
fact_audit.note: ADW: not aggressive, hides or flees, reputation of biting only if provoked (though it is territorial toward rivals). Wikipedia: flees first, bites if cornered and touched.

fact_audit.fact: Female lays one clutch of 60 to 100 eggs, broods about 50 days without eating, dies shortly after hatching
fact_audit.note: Matches ADW for H. lunulata, a student-written account. Wikipedia's genus-level figure differs (about 50 eggs, about six months, likely a different species). Keep it species-labelled and say 'about'.

fact_audit.fact: Habitat section: 'keeps a single crevice as a base to return to between hunts'
fact_audit.note: ADW says it hides in crevices, shells and discarded cans; no source found for one fixed home crevice. Soften to 'hides in crevices and empty shells'.
